canonical_json_functions.input_shape: JSON-like value; state types are expected to exclude undefined, functions, symbols, cycles, and non-finite values
canonical_json_functions.normalization_order: null/bool/string primitive handling; numbers through canonNumber; arrays recurse in supplied order; object own keys sort by JS UTF-16 lexical order before recursive emission; unsupported values fall back to null text
canonical_json_functions.output_encoding: Canonical JSON text; number zero and non-finite values emit 0, Number.isInteger values use toString, other finite numbers use toPrecision(12)
canonical_json_functions.notes: Number.isInteger is a formatting branch, not Number.isSafeInteger admission. Undefined/function/symbol are rendered as null rather than preserved as absence; wire validators reject them before authoritative commit. Arrays are never sorted by this function.

canonical_json_functions.input_shape: Pending-operation, commit-context, and envelope authoritativeState values used for re-ack equality
canonical_json_functions.normalization_order: Undefined first; null and non-object primitives through JSON.stringify(value) with undefined fallback; arrays recurse in supplied order; object own keys default-sort and recurse without dropping undefined-valued properties
canonical_json_functions.output_encoding: Deterministic comparison text that is not necessarily valid JSON: undefined emits the unquoted literal token undefined, including array members and object values
tests: No direct pure test found by rg; static source evidence only.
canonical_json_functions.notes: Native primitive JSON number semantics apply: finite fractions use JSON.stringify spelling, -0 emits 0, and NaN/Infinity emit null. An undefined object key is retained as "key":undefined.

canonical_json_functions.normalization_order: Undefined/null to null; non-finite and signed zero to 0; integer toString; fractional toPrecision(12); arrays preserve order; object keys default-sort

ordering_rules.rule: Object keys sort with default JavaScript UTF-16 lexical order; arrays preserve caller order.

Tags sort by tagType; arena tags by tagType then numeric side with counters excluded; modifiers by type ID; held items by bi, type ID, stack count; ball counts by numeric ball type; weather/terrain counters are excluded.
Final core object sorting is explicit; normalized keyed-mon entries sort by canonical entry text; modifier blobs sort by type ID then canonicalized args; arrays preserve order.
Command targets sort numerically by fieldIndex, ownerSeatId, pokemonId.
Command owners deduplicate and sort numerically; terminal and await controls have no owners.

Successor kinds deduplicate then use declared authority-kind order; interaction kinds and opaque IDs deduplicate then default-sort. Allowed interaction/control address helpers map, default-sort, and join without deduplication; accepted controls separately reject duplicate address keys during validation.
The supplied remaining sequence is preserved and occurrence values must be strictly increasing; it is not sorted by control ID.
Account IDs are validated but not normalized; exact original strings sort by default JS UTF-16 lexical order before dense seat assignment, and seat array order then remains fixed.
NFKC/lowercase normalized strings are compared with JS relational UTF-16 order; original strings are returned.
Events, roster, party, and checkpoint arrays are ordered; event owner derives from sequence parity comments/validation.
Checkpoint arrays preserve caller order; sanitization clamps/truncates but does not sort.
Native JSON.stringify preserves object construction/property insertion order and array order; this is transport encoding, not core canonical JSON.

A fixed outer object insertion order is native-JSON-stringified; nested material/nextControl/tail preserve source property and array order, while tail entry context is removed. No key sorting or hash is applied.
tests: No direct pure fingerprint test found by rg; static source evidence only.

ordering_rules.rule: Dex/starter source and output records have numeric species keys. Under JS own-property enumeration these integer-index keys enumerate ascending numerically, including during JSON.stringify({dex, starter}); this is native enumeration, not explicit core key sorting.
tests: No dedicated direct dex ordering test found by rg; static source evidence only.

ordering_rules.rule: Journal message comparisons use insertion-order JSON.stringify; snapshot mark keys are sorted before JSON.stringify.
Dataset map keys sort numerically; fixed field tuples and list array order are preserved.
Operation ID component order is epoch, owner, kind, pinned sequence, separated by literal colons.
Modifier identity concatenates typeId, className, JSON.stringify(args ?? []), and JSON.stringify(typePregenArgs ?? []) with literal pipes; nested JSON is insertion-order, not core-sorted.

FNV modifier identity preserves fixed outer array order [classNameOrNull, argsOrEmpty], then core canonicalize recursively sorts object keys and preserves nested arrays; output joins typeId and the hash with one literal space.
Arrays preserve supplied order; object own keys default-sort by JS UTF-16 lexical order; undefined-valued keys remain present with the literal value token undefined.
tests: No direct pure test found by rg; static source evidence only.

ordering_rules.rule: Pending duplicate identity compares digest and native JSON.stringify(nextControl/subsumes), preserving insertion-order structure.
Active diagnostic token labels sort with default lexical order before freezing the snapshot array.

absent_null_rules.rule: Encountered undefined/function/symbol becomes JSON null text, so this function alone cannot distinguish absent from explicit null.
Undefined, non-finite numbers, sparse holes, cycles, symbols/functions, and non-plain objects are rejected before wire entry acceptance.
JSON.stringify/JSON.parse drops undefined object properties before material digest; explicit null survives.
Absent optional fields are omitted; explicit arenaTags: [] remains present; optional form/ability/tera/status/owner fields omit when undefined.

Optional coop/endState/checkpoint remain absent when not supplied. Optional target belongs to a move command and is a BattlerIndex, not a checkpoint target; it accepts undefined or Number.isInteger, not an implicit null wildcard.
Absent data/rewardSurface are deliberately normalized to explicit null inside the fixed proposal arrays.

AWAIT_SUCCESSOR.allowedKinds is required, nonempty, and nonnullable. SHARED_INTERACTION.successor.operationIds and AWAIT_SUCCESSOR.expectedOperationId are required nullable fields whose null encodes *. Optional allowed-address helpers use addresses == null, so omission/undefined and directly supplied null both encode *; validation separately rejects explicit null because the contract permits only omission or an array. A null operationId inside an allowed control address also encodes *.

journalHighWater uses snapshot.journalHighWater ?? {} before the JSON transport round trip, so both null and undefined become {} for that field. Other undefined object properties are dropped by the round trip while explicit null survives.
Undefined is distinguished from null as the unquoted literal token undefined. Undefined array members and object values are retained rather than omitted or converted to null.
tests: No direct pure test found by rg; static source evidence only.

integer_assumptions.rule: Authoritative revisions, session epoch, membership revision, seats, and connection generation require Number.isSafeInteger; revisions are positive.
Control wave/turn/index/seat/occurrence coordinates require safe integer bounds with per-field positivity/nonnegativity.
Ledger frontiers and bounded revision windows use safe integer values and ascending revision order.
Replay accepts Number.isInteger wave/turn/slot/seq/choice/indices, which is weaker than safe-integer validation.
Operation ID numeric components use Number and Number.isInteger, not Number.isSafeInteger.
Tick/wave/turn and seat bi/partyIndex/pokemonId/array entries are checked with Number.isSafeInteger at the authoritative boundary.
Finite inputs are floor/truncated and clamped for hp/maxHp, stage, status counters, moves PP, arena turns/layers, money, weather, and terrain.

These canonicalizers use Number.isInteger, not Number.isSafeInteger, only to select formatting: integer-predicate values emit toString, finite fractions emit toPrecision(12), zero/-0 and non-finite emit 0. This is not wire admission.
FNV BigInt is internal only; dex BigInt attributes encode as exact decimal strings in JSON and restore with BigInt.
tests: No dedicated direct dex delta test found by rg; static source evidence only.

integer_assumptions.rule: No integer or safe-integer predicate is applied by these serializers. Finite fractions use native JSON.stringify number spelling, -0 emits 0, and non-finite primitive numbers emit null; upstream Authority V2 validation is the separate non-finite boundary where present.
tests: Static source evidence; no Vitest executed.

integer_assumptions.rule: Biome sourceWave and reward pin/action/surface/slot use Number.isSafeInteger. Quiz identity validates epoch, pinned, and questionIndex as safe integers and derives seq exactly. The guest-pick continuation validates only step as a safe integer and checks wave >= 0; seq/pinned are trusted inputs there. meOpAddr itself has no predicate. All are distinct from the generic operation-ID parser, which only uses Number.isInteger.

evidence: Core, turn/learn, and six other Authority V2 adapters implement separate canonical helpers.
